Private Car, Family Van or Shared Shuttle for Umrah: Which Should You Choose?

Umrah transport compared: private sedan, private SUV or van for your own group, and shared shuttles or group buses. Cost per person, comfort, Miqat stops, luggage and timing.

By Taxi Saudi Arabia Editorial TeamPublished 28 September 2026Updated 2 October 20264 min read

Quick answer

For a solo pilgrim or a couple with light luggage, a private sedan is the simplest choice. For a family of four to seven, one private SUV or van is often similar in total cost to two cars and keeps everyone and all the luggage together. Shared shuttles and group buses cost less per person but run on someone else's timetable, with fixed stops — harder with children, older relatives or a Miqat stop.

The three real options

When people say "shared van" for Umrah they usually mean one of two very different things, so it helps to separate them:

  1. A private car for your own party — sedan or SUV, nobody else on board.
  2. A private van or minibus for your own group — a bigger vehicle, still only your family or group.
  3. A shared shuttle or group bus — seats sold to unrelated passengers, often through a travel agency or hotel, running to a timetable.

We provide options 1 and 2. Every vehicle we arrange is private to your booking — we do not sell seats to strangers. Option 3 is included here because it is a genuine alternative and the right choice for some pilgrims.

Side-by-side

Private sedanPrivate SUV / vanShared shuttle / group bus
Who's on boardOnly youOnly your family or groupOther pilgrims too
Typical size3–4 passengers, 2 large bagsSUV up to 7; vans up to 7 with more luggageMany passengers
ScheduleYoursYoursFixed timetable
Miqat and prayer stopsWhen you want themWhen you want themOnly where the bus stops
Hotel doorNearest permitted point for your hotelNearest permitted point for your hotelOften a central drop-off
PriceOne fare for the carOne fare for the vehiclePer seat
Best for1–3 people, light luggageFamilies of 4–7, older relatives, lots of luggageBudget travellers, solo pilgrims comfortable with set times

When a private car is the better choice

  • One to three travellers with normal luggage.
  • Late-night or early-morning arrivals, when waiting for a shuttle after a long flight is hard.
  • You want to choose when to leave — for example, starting Umrah in the cool of the evening.

When a private van or SUV wins

  • Families of four or more. Splitting into two cars means two drivers, two arrival times and luggage spread between boots. One SUV or van keeps everyone together, and the total is often similar to two sedans.
  • Older or less mobile relatives. More space to get in and out, room for a folded wheelchair, and a single smooth journey.
  • Heavy luggage. On the way home especially — dates, gifts and Zamzam add up.
  • The Madinah–Makkah leg. Four hours plus the Miqat stop is where comfort matters most. See Madinah to Makkah by car.

For larger groups — 10, 15, 20 pilgrims — a minibus or coaster (Toyota Hiace up to 11, Toyota Coaster up to 17) keeps the group together. See group transport.

When a shared shuttle makes sense

  • You are travelling alone on a tight budget.
  • Your travel agency package already includes group transport.
  • You are comfortable with fixed times and a central drop-off.

The trade-offs: you wait for the bus to fill or leave on schedule, you stop where it stops, and you may be a long walk from your hotel at the end.

Cost: think per trip, not per seat

Private vehicles are priced per trip, not per person. The fare for a van carrying seven is one fare — so the cost per person drops as the group grows. A rough way to compare:

  • Solo traveller: a shared seat is cheapest; a private sedan costs more but saves time.
  • Couple: a private sedan is often good value for the convenience.
  • Family of four to seven: one SUV or van usually beats two sedans, and gets closer to shuttle prices per person.

Send your group size and we will compare the options for your exact route.

Questions to settle before you book

  • How many large suitcases? This decides the vehicle more often than the number of people.
  • Children's ages — and whether you need child seats.
  • Do you need a Miqat stop? Mention it so it is planned into the trip.
  • Which legs? Airport → Makkah, Makkah → Madinah, Ziyarat, back to the airport — booking them together keeps the same vehicle size throughout.

Common questions

Will strangers ever be added to my van?

No. Every booking is private to your own party, whatever the vehicle size.

Is a van more expensive than two cars?

Often not. One larger vehicle can cost about the same as two sedans, and it keeps everyone together. We'll compare both for your trip.

Can we book one vehicle for the whole Umrah trip?

Yes — airport arrival, Makkah to Madinah, Ziyarat and the airport departure can all be quoted together.
